terminal.description: The route board runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell is in your workspace if you want to look around.

tasks.title: Show which routes are ticked
tasks.description:
`renderBoard(list, routes, ticked)` now gets a `Set` of ticked route ids. Every route item already has a `<button class="tick">`. Make the board show the state:

- the button has `aria-pressed="true"` when the route's id is in `ticked`, and `aria-pressed="false"` when it is not
- the `<li class="route">` of a ticked route also has the class `ticked`
- give the button `type="button"` so it never submits anything

The check clicks one tick and reads both.
nextSteps: Read `src/main.js` to see how a click turns into a change to `ticked` and a new `render()`.
In `routeItem`, set `aria-pressed` on the button from `isTicked`.
Add or leave out the `ticked` class on the item the same way.
Save, click a tick in the Browser panel and see the button fill in.
hints: `routeItem` already receives `isTicked`. Nothing uses it yet.
`item.classList.toggle('ticked', isTicked)` adds the class when the second argument is true and removes it when it is false.

tasks.title: One listener for the whole list
tasks.description:
Staff report that the first tick works and then nothing does. `watchTicks(list, onToggle)` in `src/ticks.js` puts a listener on each button that exists when the page loads.

Rewrite it so it adds one `click` listener to `list` itself and works out which route was clicked from the event. It calls `onToggle(id)` with the `data-id` of the route whose `.tick` button was clicked, and does nothing for clicks elsewhere in the list.

The check ticks, unticks and ticks again, and it also clicks a route item that was put into the list after the page loaded.
nextSteps: Click two ticks in the Browser panel and notice that the second does nothing.
Find where the board throws away its old buttons and makes new ones.
Replace the loop with a single listener on `list`.
Inside it, find the `.tick` button the click came from, and its route.
hints: Every `render()` builds brand new buttons. The listeners were attached to the old ones, which are gone.
A click on a button bubbles up through its parents. A listener on the list hears clicks on everything inside it, now and later.
In the listener, `event.target.closest('.tick')` gives you the button, or `null` when the click was somewhere else. From the button, `closest('.route')` gives you the item and its `dataset.id`.

tasks.title: A count that stays right
tasks.description:
Write `renderCount(element, routes, ticked)` in `src/board.js`. It sets the text of `element` (the `

` in the header) to: `N of M ticked` where `M` is the number of routes and `N` is how many of those routes are in `ticked`. With no routes it reads `0 of 0 ticked`. `render()` already calls it after every change.
nextSteps: Count the routes whose id is in `ticked`.
Build the sentence with a template literal.
Tick and untick a few routes and watch the header.
hints: The count is a number made from the routes array. `filter` and `length` will do.
Count routes that are ticked, not the size of the set. Later the set may hold ids of routes that are no longer on the board.
The check compares the text exactly: a number, the word `of`, a number and the word `ticked`, with single spaces and nothing else.
